title: OpenSpiel GUI contract
description: Version 7 of the contract. Every response body is one of these; request bodies are among the definitions. Generated by schema.py; do not edit.

Action.description: A legal action at a position.

id.description: The OpenSpiel action id, which a client sends to play it.

label.description: The game's text for the action.

ActionHint.description: What a game's adapter says about one legal action, for its renderer.

hint.description: The adapter's description of the action, such as the card it plays or the cells it joins.

Advance.description:
Lets controllers play their seats.

Play stops when a human seat or an exposed chance node must act, the game ends, a controller fails, or `max_plies` seat actions have been applied. Under the `auto` policy, chance outcomes are sampled as they come and do not count.

One request holds its session until play stops, so play is bounded.

max_plies.description: The most seat actions to apply, from 1 to 1000, or null for 1000.

ApplyAction.description: Plays an action for the seat to move.

action.description: The OpenSpiel action id, one of the frame's `legal_actions`.

ply.description: The position to play at, the `ply` of the frame the action was chosen from: null, or `num_plies`, for the live position. An earlier ply plays from that position and takes back every later ply, as only an omniscient viewer may.

ApplyChanceOutcome.description: Chooses the outcome at a chance node under the `expose` policy.

outcome.description: The OpenSpiel action id, one of the frame's `chance_outcomes`.

ply.description: The position to choose at, as for `ApplyAction`.

Capabilities.description: What the server can do, independent of any one game.

controllers.description: Every registered controller, starting with the human one.

chance_policies.description: The chance policies the server accepts.

cpp_mcts_limits.description: How the served pyspiel's C++ MCTS bounds a search, and so which limits MCTS plays with.

contract_version.description: The contract version the catalogue was built against.

games.description: One entry per game, ordered by name.

CatalogueEntry.description: A game the server knows, and whether it can serve it.

name.description: The game's short name, which a client sends to create a session.

min_seats.description: The fewest seats the game supports.

max_seats.description: The most seats the game supports.

num_players.description: The number of seats the game has with its default parameters, between `min_seats` and `max_seats`; null when not loadable.

parameters.description: The game's parameters, ordered by name.

loadable.description: Whether the server can serve the game.

unavailable_reason.description: Why the server cannot serve the game; null when loadable.

controllers.description: The `Controller.name`s that can play the game with its default parameters; empty when not loadable.

renderer.description: The renderer its frames name in `Presentation.renderer`, from the game's registered adapter: the board a client draws it with, if the client has that renderer. Null for a game with no adapter, and for one that is not loadable; such a game is shown as its text.

ChanceMode.description:
How the game uses chance, as the game declares it.

- `deterministic`: The game has no chance nodes.
- `explicit_stochastic`: Chance nodes list their outcomes and probabilities.
- `sampled_stochastic`: Chance outcomes are sampled inside the state.

ChanceOutcome.description: A chance outcome at a chance node.

id.description: The OpenSpiel action id, which a client sends to choose it.

label.description: The game's text for the outcome.

ChancePolicy.description:
How chance nodes are resolved.

- `auto`: The server samples each outcome from a seeded generator.
- `expose`: The client chooses each outcome; in a game that hides information, only from the oracle view.

Controller.description: A kind of agent that can play a seat.

name.description: The stable identifier used in requests and in `SeatView.controller`.

config_schema.description: A JSON Schema object that a seat's `config` for this controller must satisfy; `{}` when it takes no settings. Each of its `properties` gives a setting's `type`, `default` and constraints; a setting listed in its `required` has no `default`, and a seat must be given it.

unavailable_reason.description: Why the controller cannot play the session's game; null when it can. A seat is never played by a controller with a reason.

ControllerFailure.description: Why a seat's controller stopped playing.

error.description: The name of the exception the controller raised.

message.description: The exception's message; null for every viewer that is not omniscient, the failing seat included, since the message may describe any seat's private state.

parameters.description: Game parameters; omitted ones take their defaults.

seats.description: Who plays each seat, in seat order, one per seat of the game.

seed.description: The chance generator's seed, a non-negative integer, or null for the server to choose one.

Dynamics.description:
How players move, as the game declares it.

- `sequential`: One player acts at a time.
- `simultaneous`: Players act together; served through the turn-based wrapper.
- `mean_field`: A mean-field game.

contract_version.description: The contract version the error was built against.

message.description: A human-readable explanation, safe to show the requester: it never holds state the requester may not see.

seat.description: The seat the refusal concerns, or null.

ply.description: The index of the history entry the refusal concerns, or null.

ErrorCode.description:
Why a request was refused.

- `bad_request`: The request is malformed.
- `not_found`: The session, game, seat or ply does not exist.
- `method_not_allowed`: The path exists but does not accept the method.
- `game_unavailable`: The game cannot be served; its catalogue entry says why.
- `viewer_unavailable`: The game cannot build a frame for the viewer.
- `not_your_turn`: The viewer may not choose the next action.
- `illegal_action`: The action is not legal at the position.
- `controller_unavailable`: The controller cannot play the game, or its settings do not satisfy its `config_schema`.
- `controller_failed`: A seat's controller failed and the session is paused.
- `nothing_to_undo`: The live game has no action to undo.

Frame.description:
A position of a session, built for one viewer.

A frame is live when `ply == num_plies`, and a replay of an earlier position otherwise. A seat acts at the live position; an omniscient viewer may also play from a replay, which takes back the plies after it.

contract_version.description: The contract version the frame was built against.

viewer.description: The audience the frame is built for.

omniscient.description: Whether the viewer sees the full state: exactly when the viewer is the oracle or the game hides nothing (`session.hides_information` is false).

status.description: The state of the session's live game.

ply.description: The number of actions, chance outcomes included, applied to reach this position.

num_plies.description: The number of actions in the live game.

legal_actions.description: The actions the acting seat may choose; empty where no seat acts and, for a viewer that is not omniscient, on a replay; null when withheld from the viewer.

chance_outcomes.description: The outcomes the client may choose at a chance node under the `expose` policy; empty otherwise, null when withheld from the viewer.

history.description: Every action of the live game, in order, as the viewer may see it.

rewards.description: Each seat's reward for the action that reached this position, in seat order; null at the initial position or when that action is withheld from the viewer.

returns.description: Each seat's return, in seat order, at a terminal position; otherwise null.

state_text.description: The full state as text; null unless `omniscient`.

observation_text.description: The viewer's observation as text; null unless the viewer holds a seat and the game provides observations.

information_state_text.description: The viewer's information state as text; null unless the viewer holds a seat and the game provides information states.

struct.description: The full state as the game's structured JSON; null unless `omniscient` and the game provides it.

observation_struct.description: The viewer's observation as the game's structured JSON; null unless the viewer holds a seat and the game provides observation structs.

presentation.description: The position as the game's adapter presents it to the viewer; null when no adapter is registered for the game.

contract_version.description: The contract version the server speaks.

revision.description: The source revision the server runs from, or null when unknown.

HistoryEntry.description: One action of the live game, as the viewer may see it.

seat.description: The seat that acted, or null for a chance outcome.

action.description: The OpenSpiel action id, or null when withheld from the viewer.

label.description: The game's text for the action, or null when withheld.

rewards.description: Each seat's reward for the action, in seat order, or null when withheld.

public_label.description: What every viewer may read of a withheld action, as the game's adapter says, such as a card discarded face up; null when the action is shown in full or wholly hidden.

Information.description:
What the players observe, as the game declares it.

- `one_shot`: A one-shot game.
- `perfect_information`: Every player observes the full state.
- `imperfect_information`: Some state is hidden from some players.

MctsLimits.description:
How the served pyspiel's C++ MCTS (`pyspiel.MCTSBot`) bounds a search.

The server finds out once, at startup, and picks MCTS's limits by it.

- `simulations_or_clock`: A search stops at its simulation count or its wall-clock time, whichever comes first. MCTS runs up to 10000 simulations, 1000 by default, with a wall-clock backstop a little inside the move budget.
- `simulations_only`: A wall-clock time replaces the simulation count rather than bounding it. MCTS sets no wall-clock time, and its simulations are capped at 250, which fits the move budget on the slowest catalogued game.

MoverKind.description:
Who acts at a position.

- `seat`: A seat chooses the next action.
- `chance`: Chance chooses the next action.
- `terminal`: The game is over and nobody acts.

ParameterKind.description:
Which values a game parameter admits.

- `free`: Any value of its type.
- `range`: A number between `minimum` and `maximum`, inclusive.
- `choice`: One of `choices`.

ParameterSpec.description: A game parameter, as a client needs it to offer the parameter.

name.description: The parameter's name, a key of a session's `parameters`.

type.description: The type of the parameter's value.

default.description: The value the game uses when none is given.

minimum.description: The least admitted value when `kind` is `range`, otherwise null.

maximum.description: The greatest admitted value when `kind` is `range`, otherwise null.

choices.description: The admitted values when `kind` is `choice`, otherwise null.

description.description: What the parameter controls, or null when the game does not say.

ParameterType.description:
The type of a game parameter's value.

- `bool`: A boolean.
- `int`: An integer.
- `float`: A real number.
- `string`: A string.

Presentation.description: A position as the game's adapter presents it to one viewer.

renderer.description: The name of the client renderer that draws the view.

view.description: The adapter's view of the position, holding only what the viewer may see.

actions.description: The adapter's hints for the legal actions, each naming an action of the frame's `legal_actions` at most once; null exactly when the frame's `legal_actions` is null.

Reset.description: Restarts the live game, keeping the session's seats.

history.description: Actions to replay from the initial state, chance outcomes included, as in a frame's `history`; null or empty for a fresh game.

autoplay.description: Whether the server plays the seat's moves as soon as it is to move. Must be false for a human seat.

SeatStatus.description:
Whether a seat's controller is ready to play.

- `ready`: The controller is built and plays the seat; a human seat is always ready.
- `preparing`: The server is building the controller, which can take a while (a trained model loads and warms up). The seat does not move until it is ready; then autoplay goes on.
- `unavailable`: The controller could not be built, or was not built within the build budget. The seat has a `failure`, so the session is paused until the seat is given a controller again.

seat.description: The seat index, which is the OpenSpiel player id.

config.description: The controller's settings, satisfying its `config_schema`. Every viewer receives them, so they hold no secret.

autoplay.description: Whether the server plays the seat's moves as soon as it is to move, rather than on an advance request. Never true for a human seat.

failure.description: Why the controller failed, or null while it plays.

status.description: Whether the controller is ready, being built, or could not be built.

message.description: Why the seat is not ready, for every viewer: what the server is doing while it is `preparing`, or why it is `unavailable`; null when it is `ready`, and optional while it is `preparing`.

SessionInfo.description: The fixed properties of a session.

turn_based.description: Whether a simultaneous game is served through the turn-based wrapper, which has its seats act one after another.

hides_information.description: Whether some seat may not see the full state. When false, every viewer is omniscient.

seed.description: The chance generator's seed; null for every viewer but the oracle, since it determines every chance outcome to come.

controllers.description: The controllers that can play a seat of this game.

SessionStatus.description:
The state of a session's live game.

- `playing`: The game is in progress.
- `paused`: A seat's controller failed; play resumes only after an undo, a reset or a change of that seat's controller. A seat whose controller could not be built (`SeatStatus.UNAVAILABLE`) resumes only after a change of its controller.
- `terminal`: The game is over.

kind.description: Whether a seat or chance acts, or the game is over.

seat.description: The acting seat when `kind` is `seat`, otherwise null.

Viewer.description: The audience a frame is built for.

kind.description: Whether the viewer holds a seat, watches, or sees everything.

seat.description: The viewer's seat when `kind` is `seat`, otherwise null.

ViewerKind.description:
Who a frame is built for.

- `seat`: A player, who sees what that player may observe.
- `spectator`: A watcher in no seat, who sees only public state.
- `oracle`: An omniscient observer, who sees the full state.
